text:
alejandra: Quick follow-up on the interface consolidation RFC — can we land on a concrete plan for the data-plane facade this quarter? I sketched a small proposal.
alejandra: TL;DR: collapse 3 thin adapters (session-router, enrich, kv-proxy) into one stable facade with feature flags for per-tenant routing. reduces cross-service contracts and router churn.
matt: sketch please — worried about surface area. we had perf problems when we tried merging adapters last year.
alejandra: sure — gist of the API:
```
POST /v1/infer
{ tenant_id, model, input, trace_id }
```
internal header X-RW-Route: {hotpath|async|batch}
Facade handles routing -> picks runtime, or falls back to cheaper quantized variant.
ryan: ok but how do we keep rollout small? can we preserve adapter-level ownership for a while?
sara: propose a phased approach: 1) facade read-only pass-through (no routing changes) 2) add routing decision in facade behind flag 3) migrate one tenant group to facade routing 4) flip routing for all
matt: +1 phased. also add per-tenant timeout and quota enforcement at facade layer to avoid blast radius.
alejandra: yep. infra-bot ran a quick load projection: merging adapters reduces p99 by ~6% for cross-service calls (simulated). pasted numbers below.
infra-bot: simulated RPC hops: 3 -> 1, average serialization overhead saved ~0.9ms/request, KV-cache locality improves hit-rate by estimated 3-5%.
ryan: what about deployment topology? if facade is stateful for session affinity we need sticky routing or sidecar changes.
sara: keep facade stateless. session affinity handled via a short-lived session token that maps to runtime; we already have session-mapper service — move mapping store to dedicated redis cluster attached to DEDICATED capacity nodes.
matt: that means Dedicated customers need network peering to reach Redis. Ops impact but acceptable.
alejandra: ownership: arch team owns the facade API and rollout plan; adapters' teams keep impls until migration done. we'll create a migration checklist.
ryan: checklist item: automated smoke tests that compare outputs (token-by-token diff) for migrated tenants, with a threshold for divergence.
sara: also add a canary watcher that measures cost delta (tokens/ms) and quality regression (BLEU/ROUGE or eval harness metrics) every hour.
alejandra: sounds good. action items:
- matt: define quota/timeouts to enforce at facade (due EOD Tue)
- ryan: add smoke test harness and diff tool (due Fri)
- sara: cost/quality watcher + dashboards (sync with obs) (due next Wed)
- alejandro (me): draft migration runbook and feature-flag plan (PR tomorrow)
matt: noted. one more question: rollback strategy? how easy to revert if we see Q drop?
sara: revert flag + immediate traffic re-route to old adapters. keep old adapters running 14 days after cutover.
ryan: also keep a short-term side-by-side run mode where we send traffic to both and compare latency; only promote when variance < 2.5% p95.
alejandra: perfect. I'll open RFC follow-up with the checklist and owners. pinging @matt @ryan @sara for final approvals.
matt: approved from infra POV :thumbsup:
ryan: approved from runtime POV :ok_hand:
sara: approved from product/delivery :raised_hands:
alejandra: thanks. I'll schedule a 30m sync to go over the runbook tomorrow.
